testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: If your brakes lose hydraulic pressure, which of the following should you NOT do?
questions.explanation: If your brakes lose hydraulic pressure, downshift, pump the brakes, and use the parking brake. Look for a way to escape, such as an escape ramp, open field, or side street.

questions.question: When checking power steering fluid during a vehicle inspection, which of the following is NOT required?

options.text: Show where the power steering fluid dipstick is located.
Check that there is enough power steering fluid.
Make sure the power steering fluid level is above the full mark.
Make sure the power steering level is above the refill mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the power steering fluid level is above the full mark.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must show where the power steering fluid dipstick is and prove there is enough power steering fluid. The fluid level must be above the refill mark, not above the full mark.

questions.question: What was the purpose of front brake limiting valves?

options.text: Stop the front tires from skidding.
Stop the front tires from overheating.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the front tires from skidding.
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles with air brakes have front brake limiting valves. They were designed to prevent the front wheels from skidding. However, research shows these devices are not needed, so they should be left in the normal position.

questions.question: Friction in a brake drum happens when the brake shoes and linings:

options.text: Push against the inside of the drum.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push against the inside of the drum.
questions.explanation: Friction in a brake drum is created when the brake shoes and linings push against the inside of the drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a good way to reduce crashes when turning right?

options.text: Keep the back of your vehicle close to the curb.
Leave open space on your right side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave open space on your right side.
questions.explanation: When turning right, do not turn too wide to the left. If you need to swing into another lane, keep the back of your vehicle close to the curb. Leaving space on your right while turning right may confuse other drivers into thinking you are turning left, and they may try to pass you on the right.

questions.question: When it is hard for others to see your vehicle at dawn or dusk, you can help by:

options.text: Waving your arm out the window.

questions.explanation: When visibility is low, turn your headlights on to the low beam setting. If you have trouble seeing others, they have trouble seeing you.

questions.question: On the on-road test, you will be checked on traffic awareness. You should NOT:

options.text: Skip checking your mirrors near intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Skip checking your mirrors near intersections.
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, check for traffic and use your mirrors regularly, especially at intersections. Look for pedestrians wherever they may be present.

questions.question: What is black ice?

options.text: A thick layer of ice on the road.
A thin layer of ice on the road.
Ice that is black from dirt on the road.
Ice that is easy to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: A thin layer of ice on the road.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice on the road. You can see the road surface through it. A road with black ice may look wet rather than icy.

questions.question: Foundation brakes are used:

options.text: Only at the driver's side wheels.

questions.explanation: Foundation brakes are used at all four wheels. The most common type is the S-cam drum brake.

questions.question: How many driver's licenses can a person have?

options.text: Two—one for cars and one for trucks.
One for each state where they plan to drive.
A regular license from one state and a CDL from another.

questions.explanation: A person cannot have more than one license. States share driver information through a computer database to prevent duplicate licenses.

questions.question: When traction is poor, why should a driver accelerate slowly?

options.text: Because it is always best to accelerate slowly.
To avoid losing control of the vehicle.
So you do not go faster than the vehicle ahead.
To be the last vehicle through an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: To avoid losing control of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Speeding up too quickly on slippery roads can cause you to lose control. When traction is poor, accelerate slowly and smoothly.

questions.question: During an inspection, brake pads should be:
questions.explanation: Brake pads and shoes must not have oil, grease, or brake fluid on them.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a backing maneuver on the basic control skills test?
questions.explanation: The basic control skills test includes straight line backing, offset back/right, offset back/left, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking. Blind offset is not included.

questions.question: For a single vehicle with air brakes, what is the maximum leakage rate during an applied leakage test?
questions.explanation: A single vehicle with air brakes should have no more than 3 psi of air loss in one minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: What does ABS do?

options.text: Prevent the air compressor from overheating
Prevent the front brakes from being used on ice
Prevent the brakes from being used if downshifting would be more effective

questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents wheels from locking up when you brake hard, especially on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: Why are roads slippery when it first begins to rain?

options.text: Fresh rain mixes with oil on the road.
The water has nowhere to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fresh rain mixes with oil on the road.
questions.explanation: When it first rains, the water mixes with oil and grease on the road, creating a slippery film. As rain continues, this mixture washes away.

questions.question: If you exit your vehicle incorrectly during the basic control skills test, what happens?

options.text: You automatically fail the entire basic control skills test.
You receive an extra point against your score.

questions.correctAnswerText: You automatically fail the entire basic control skills test.
questions.explanation: You must face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times when exiting. For a bus, you must hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly results in automatic failure of the entire test.

questions.question: To help others see your vehicle, headlights should be:
questions.explanation: Keep your headlights clean so they produce as much light as possible. This helps other drivers see your vehicle at night.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Increase the space in front of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the space in front of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Create more space in front of your vehicle. This makes it easier for the tailgater to pass you safely. Speeding up will not help because they may just tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: When checking the engine compartment, which of the following should you NOT check?

options.text: The coolant level in the radiator.

questions.explanation: Check the oil level, coolant level, hose condition, power steering fluid, windshield washer fluid, battery connections and fluid, automatic transmission fluid, belt condition, and any leaks or damaged wiring. The fuel level is checked at the fuel gauge, not in the engine compartment.

questions.question: During exercises other than straight line backing, how many times can you exit your vehicle to check its position?
questions.explanation: You can exit your vehicle to check its position during basic control skills tests. This is called a "look." For straight line backing, you may look only one time. For all other exercises, you may look two times.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, check that spring brakes come on automatically when:
questions.explanation: Spring brakes should come on automatically when air tank pressure falls between 20 and 45 psi. Test this by chocking the wheels and releasing air by pressing the brake pedal repeatedly. When pressure gets too low, the parking brake valve will pop out and spring brakes will activate.

questions.question: For a triple combination air brake vehicle, the maximum air leakage during a static test is ____ per minute.
questions.explanation: On a triple combination air brake vehicle, air leakage during a static test must not exceed 5 psi per minute. If leakage is faster than this, do not drive the vehicle. Something needs repair.

questions.question: When using mirrors while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Look in the mirrors for long periods.
Use only the driver's side mirror.

questions.explanation: Looking at mirrors for too long is dangerous. You will travel far without watching the road ahead.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: You do not need to use a turn signal.

questions.explanation: Change lanes slowly and smoothly. This keeps your vehicle under control and gives other drivers time to move away. Always use your turn signal to tell other drivers your plans.

questions.question: A low air pressure warning signal should turn on when:
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, a low air pressure warning must activate when tank pressure drops below 60 psi. The warning can be a light, a buzzer, or a wig wag.

questions.question: When driving, what should you do?

options.text: Use turn signals only if vehicles are near you.
Do not use turn signals in construction zones.
Always use turn signals to warn others about your plans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use turn signals to warn others about your plans.
questions.explanation: Tell other drivers what you plan to do. Signal before turning or changing lanes, even if no other vehicles are nearby.

questions.question: Why is it most important to inspect your vehicle before a trip?
questions.explanation: The most important reason to inspect your vehicle is to keep yourself and others safe. State and federal laws require safety inspections before every trip.

questions.question: How can you avoid becoming drowsy while driving?

options.text: Get about three hours of sleep beforehand.
Plan ahead and include stopping points.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan ahead and include stopping points.
questions.explanation: To reduce drowsiness while driving, get seven to eight hours of sleep before your trip. Drive during times you are normally awake. Plan breaks during your trip. Exercise regularly.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, you need to check all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: During a vehicle inspection, check the power steering belt, water pump belt, alternator belt, and air compressor belt for snugness, cracks, or fraying. If any part is not belt-driven, tell the examiner which one and confirm it works properly, is mounted securely, and is not damaged or leaking.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate for a triple combination vehicle during a leakage test?
questions.explanation: You need to know the safe air loss rate for your vehicle. A triple combination vehicle cannot lose more than 6 psi per minute during a leakage test.

questions.question: Why should you cover your cargo?

options.text: To prevent other drivers from seeing what you are transporting

questions.explanation: Cover your cargo to protect people if it spills and to protect the cargo from weather.

questions.question: When driving with a load, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and check the cargo within the first 50 miles
Ask other drivers about their load condition
Use only the side mirrors to check the cargo
Skip checking the cargo if it was secured properly at the start

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and check the cargo within the first 50 miles
questions.explanation: Check your cargo before you start driving. Then check it again within the first 50 miles, every three hours or 150 miles, and after each break.

questions.question: If you realize you may be late to your destination, what should you do?

options.text: Use flashing lights so other drivers move out of your way
Drive safely and arrive when you arrive

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive safely and arrive when you arrive
questions.explanation: Stay calm and drive safely. Do not rush or drive dangerously. Plan ahead for possible delays to reduce stress about arriving late.

questions.question: When checking automatic transmission fluid, what might you need to do?

options.text: Park the vehicle on an uphill slope
Park the vehicle on a downhill slope

questions.explanation: Some vehicles require you to check the automatic transmission fluid while the engine is running.

questions.question: A pre-trip inspection has how many basic steps?
questions.explanation: There are seven basic steps: overview of the vehicle, check the engine compartment, start the engine and check inside the cab, turn off the engine and check the lights, walk around the vehicle, check the signal lights, and start the engine to check the brakes.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of drowsiness?
questions.explanation: Signs of drowsiness include frequent blinking, eyes closing or losing focus on their own, frequent yawning, and drifting between lanes. Feeling hungry is not a sign of drowsiness.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate for a double combination vehicle during a leakage test?
questions.explanation: You need to know the safe air loss rate for your vehicle. A double combination vehicle cannot lose more than 4 psi per minute during a leakage test.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation in your personal car, what must you do?

options.text: The officer will tell your employer
Your CDL is not affected because the violation is on your personal license
Tell your employer within six months

questions.explanation: You must notify your employer within 30 days of any traffic violation conviction, regardless of which vehicle you were driving. This rule does not apply to parking violations.

questions.question: How can you make your vehicle more visible at dawn or dusk?
questions.explanation: At dawn, dusk, and in snow or rain, turn on your headlights so other drivers can see your vehicle.

questions.question: What happens if you don't drain the tanks in an air brake system?

options.text: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.
questions.explanation: Air brake tanks must be drained to remove water and oil. If you don't drain them, water can build up and freeze in cold weather, which causes the brakes to fail.

questions.question: How should you hold the steering wheel when driving?

options.text: With both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.
With both hands at the bottom of the wheel.
With both hands at the top of the wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: With both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: What does the service brake system do?

options.text: Applies and releases the brakes when you press the brake pedal during normal driving.
Applies and releases the parking brakes.
Applies and releases the emergency brake.
Applies and releases the axle brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Applies and releases the brakes when you press the brake pedal during normal driving.
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three separate parts: the service brake system, the parking brake system, and the emergency brake system. The service brake system applies and releases the brakes when you use the brake pedal while driving normally.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through fog?
questions.explanation: When driving in fog, use your low beam headlights.

questions.question: Which is NOT another name for convex mirrors?
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors are also called "fisheye," "spot," or "bug-eye" mirrors. Flat side mirrors are not another name for convex mirrors.

questions.question: If you drive a truck that requires a CDL, when must you wear a seat belt?

options.text: You do not need to wear a seat belt.
Only if you are carrying more than 500 pounds of cargo.
Only when driving a tank trailer.

questions.explanation: For safety, you must always wear your seat belt when operating a commercial motor vehicle.

questions.question: Which braking system includes the brake pedal?
questions.explanation: The service brake system applies and releases the brakes when you press the brake pedal during normal driving.

questions.question: What is another name for front-end header boards?
questions.explanation: Front-end header boards are also called "headache racks." They protect the driver from cargo if it shifts during a crash or emergency stop.

questions.question: How should you hold the steering wheel?

options.text: With one hand so you can eat and drink.
With one hand at a time, alternating between hands.

questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides of the wheel to maintain proper control of your vehicle.

questions.question: When driving at highway speeds, how far ahead should you watch the road?
questions.explanation: Watch the road 12 to 15 seconds ahead of your vehicle to see upcoming obstacles and hazards. At highway speeds, this equals about one quarter mile.
